reference_frame.description: Stone corridor receding north (+y) to a vanishing point, converging side walls, textured floor+ceiling, green portcullis/gate at the far end. Re-confirmed game_state=5 facing=0 z=0 y=3 x=7 gx=127 gy=119 this run.
reference_frame.viewport: x72..247 (w176) y32..143 (h112) in the 320x200 framebuffer (from wmaze-3d-view.json, unchanged).

summary: Filled the remaining gap from wmaze-3d-view.json: the per-slot blit GEOMETRY of the first-person view. KEY ARCHITECTURE CORRECTION: the view is NOT a set of fixed sprite-blit rectangles. It is an EDGE-LIST TEXTURED-POLYGON rasterizer. view_render_corridor_frame (0x4ad7) runs a back-to-front depth loop (depth 0..3, [0x5040]); per depth it classifies 5 slots (center/front 0x3828(0), corner 0x3c11(0), overlay 0x3dce(0), left-side 0x3828(0xffff), right-side 0x3828(1)) into wall-type codes stored at [0x5220/0x5222/0x5224/0x5226/0x5228], then runs gated draw blocks. Each draw block pushes a STATIC table of screen-X immediates (the per-slot polygon vertex columns) and calls one of three polygon emitters: wall_emit_quad (0x406c, 35 args, a 15-way shape jump-table on the wall-type), wall_emit_corner (0x45b4, 16 args), or wall_emit_floorceil (0x47a3, 8 args). Those emitters append left/right edge spans to a span list at 0x50d0.. (counter 0x50ce, max 30) via span_append (0x3f8d), each span tagged with the wall-type for texture lookup; when the list fills (or at end of frame) it flushes through a wroot draw thunk (0xc546) and the per-region clip is set via 0xf148. Floor & ceiling are drawn FIRST as two full-window image_blit backgrounds (0x42 -> 0xbb9a, per-zone far-ptr tables [bx+0x7d2]/[bx+0x80a], bx=zone*4; zone0 floor asset id=0x542=1346, ceiling id=0x6cc=1740) before any wall spans. The wall-type code (0/2 in the static corridor; 0=open/no-draw, 2=solid stone) selects BOTH the polygon SHAPE (via 0x406c's jump table) and the TEXTURE (span_append tags each span with wall-type, used to index the per-type texture/clip column tables at 0x36e4/0x3717). All vertex-column immediates and the shape jump-table were read directly from the binary (ndisasm) and the wall-type codes + maze-bit grid were read live from the reference frame.

findings.claim: The first-person view is an edge-list textured-polygon rasterizer, NOT a fixed-rectangle sprite compositor. Per visible slot the renderer pushes a static table of screen-X vertex columns and calls a polygon emitter (0x406c quad / 0x45b4 corner / 0x47a3 floor-ceiling fill) that appends spans to a list at 0x50d0.. and flushes via a wroot draw thunk.

evidence.details: Depth-loop body 0x4d95..0x51ec. Per depth (bx=[0x5040]) it tests a gate byte then pushes an immediate column table and calls 0x406c/0x45b4/0x47a3. Gates: front=[bx+0x508a], corner-left=[bx+0x508a] (via 0x45b4@0x4e61), corner-right=[bx+0x508a] (0x45b4@0x4ebd), center-floorceil=[bx+0x5082] (0x47a3@0x4ef9), left-side=[bx+0x5072] (0x406c@0x4f9b), left-side-2=[bx+0x507a] (0x406c@0x504b), right-side=[bx+0x5092] (0x406c@0x50fb), right-side-2=[bx+0x509a] (0x406c@0x51ab), right-floorceil=[bx+0x50a2] (0x47a3@0x51e7). After each emitter the per-slot wall classifier post-pass is called (0x4892/0x48f5/0x4926/0x4957/0x4984/0x49b6/0x49e8). span_append (0x3f8d) writes one entry per call to 0x50d0..0x50da (fields: x-index byte @+8, two left x words @+0/+2, walltype byte @+9, two right x words @+4/+6, flag @+a), increments [0x50ce], and when it reaches 0x1e (30) flushes via push 0; call 0xc546 (a wroot draw thunk) repeatedly until drained.

findings.claim: The per-slot polygon vertex columns are STATIC immediates pushed at each draw call site. They are screen-X columns (window-relative additions are applied inside the emitter via +[bp+4]). Tables decoded below per slot/emitter.

evidence.details: Extracted by parsing the push sequence before each emitter call and reversing push order to C-arg offsets. [bp+0x4]=slot/position param (depth or bias 0/1/2), [bp+0x6]=wall-type code ([0x5220]/[0x5226]/[0x5228]), [bp+0x8]=second control. Remaining args are the screen-X vertex columns of the polygon. The emitter adds [bp+4] (perspective bias) to selected columns and emits left/right edges via span_append/0xf148.

CENTER_floorceil (0x47a3 @0x4ef9, gate [.note: center floor/ceiling fill quad for the slot

LEFT_side_A (0x406c @0x4f9b, gate [bx+0x.indexed: one arg is [bx+0x42] (depth-indexed Y/X word array)

evidence.note: LEFT/RIGHT side tables are mirror images of each other (e.g. 130/142 vs 142/130; 181/190 vs 190/181), confirming the L/R symmetry around the corridor center. Columns >320 (329,332,335,338,341) are pre-clip; 0xf148 / the span clipper bounds them to the x72..247 viewport. Many small values (3,6,9,12,...) are the FAR-depth near-vanishing-point columns; large values (~330) are the NEAR-depth screen edges. The +[bp+4] bias and the [0x521a]/[0x521c] parity bits swap which side is emitted first (alternating-parity draw order from wmaze-3d-view.json).

findings.claim: The side-wall emitters take one depth-indexed coordinate from word arrays at DGROUP 0x42 (left, [bx+0x42]) and 0x4a (right, [bx+0x4a]), bx=depth*2. Live values: array@0x42 = {0x0000, 0x0068, 0x0080, 0x0090} for depths 0..3 (i.e. 0,104,128,144). These are the depth-scaled wall heights/Y offsets that make the corridor converge.

evidence.details: 0x406c side calls do `D1E3 shl bx,1` (bx=depth*2) then `push [bx+0x42]` (left) or `push [bx+0x4a]` (right). Live read of DGROUP 0x40..0x70 at the reference frame: bytes 40..= `00 00 00 00 68 00 80 00 90 00 ...` so word[0x42]=0, word[0x44]=0x68, word[0x46]=0x80, word[0x48]=0x90; the 0x4a array overlaps/continues. These are screen-coordinate constants (heights/offsets), NOT pointers — confirmed by their small magnitudes and direct push as the y-extent arg.

findings.claim: wall_emit_quad (0x406c) dispatches on the wall-type code [bp+6] through a 15-entry CS-relative jump table at file 0x449e (the `2e ff a7 028a` dispatch at 0x44c4, disp16 0x8a02, delta 0x4564 -> file 0x449e). Type 0 and 2 -> common path 0x44c9 (the straightforward solid-wall quad); types 1/3/4 -> 0x4101 (a wall with a door/recess variant keyed on [0x363e]); 5..13 -> distinct edge variants; 14 -> 0x4474. Each variant chooses which subset of the pushed columns become the left/right polygon edges.

evidence.details: Jump table decoded (CS off -> file off): [0]=0x8a2d->0x44c9, [1]=0x8665->0x4101, [2]=0x8a2d->0x44c9, [3]=0x8665->0x4101, [4]=0x8665->0x4101, [5]=0x87e4->0x4280, [6]=0x8818->0x42b4, [7]=0x884c->0x42e8, [8]=0x8873->0x430f, [9]=0x88d5->0x4371, [10..13]=0x8918->0x43b4, [14]=0x89d8->0x4474. Entries 0-14 all land inside 0x406c's body, re-confirming the wmaze 0x4564 CS->file delta. The static corridor only uses type 0 (open, no quad) and type 2 (solid stone) — so the SHAPE used in the reference frame is the 0x44c9 common path.

findings.claim: The wall classifier helpers (0x3828/0x3c11/0x3dce) return a small wall-type code per slot. In the static corridor the live slot array [0x5220..0x5228] held codes 0 and 2 (0=open passage -> emitter early-returns / no quad; 2=solid stone wall -> common quad shape + stone texture). The same 2-bit maze-data wall field value (0/2/3) maps onto these codes.

evidence.details: Live read at reference frame: 0x5220 region = `00 00 00 00 00 00 02 00 02 00 16 81 ...`. The first depths classified as 0 (open, looking down the empty corridor) with 2 (solid stone) appearing for the side walls / the far gate cell. wall_emit_quad's gate `cmp byte [bx+0x5042],0` and the type-0 jump-table slot landing on the empty 0x44c9 tail confirm type 0 = no-draw. CAVEAT: the precise 0-vs-2-vs-3 -> code mapping inside 0x3828 was not hand-traced; codes observed are 0 and 2.

findings.claim: span_append (0x3f8d) tags each emitted span with the wall-type [bp+a] and uses it to index per-type texture/clip column tables at DGROUP 0x36e4 (`x0`) and 0x3717 (`x1`) via wtype*0x13a. For wall-type the live tables held screen-column run values, e.g. 0x36e4: `00 90 90 8c 8c 85 85 94 94 8c 8c 88 88 94 94` and a second run `4a 43 3b 48 3e 3d 46` at 0x371b; 0x3717 mirrors with `00 4a 43 3b 48 3e 3d 46`. These are the per-type texture-edge/clip columns the rasterizer interpolates between — i.e. the perspective texture-mapping seam columns, not mazedata sprite indices.

evidence.details: 0x3f8d: `mov ax,0x13a; imul [bp+4]` (stride 0x13a per index) then `+[bp+a]` indexes [bx+0x36e4] and [bx+0x3717]; results add into the span's two stored x words (0x50d0/0x50d2). 0x13a=314 ~ a per-row stride. Live tables dumped above. The actual TEXTURE PIXELS (the stone pattern) come from the mazedata.* graphics blob via image_blit at flush time; that pixel decode is unresolved (see unresolved).

findings.claim: Floor and ceiling are drawn FIRST as two full-window image_blit backgrounds (before any wall span), in view_load_zone_and_fill (0x42). The per-zone floor asset (id at 0x3304) and ceiling asset (id at 0x3306) are decompressed via the wroot asset loader (0xf4be) into DGROUP near-ptrs 0x4faa (floor) / 0x4fa8 (ceiling), then blitted via image_blit (0xbb9a -> wroot image 0xfe) using far-pointer pairs from [bx+0x7d2]/[bx+0x7d4] (floor) and [bx+0x80a]/[bx+0x80c] (ceiling), bx=zone*4. Zone 0: floor id=0x542=1346, ceiling id=0x6cc=1740.

evidence.details: 0x42 disasm: lazy-load floor/ceiling to 0x4faa/0x4fa8 from ids 0x3304/0x3306 via 0xf4be; then two 0xbb9a (image_blit) calls with src far ptrs from the 0x7d2/0x80a tables. Live at reference frame: 0x3304=0x542, 0x3306=0x6cc; floor near-ptr 0x4faa=0x7504, ceiling 0x4fa8=0x7a48; floor blit src far ptr (zone0) seg=0x783f off=0; ceiling seg=0x7895 off=0. The blit dest (full-window) is encoded in the loaded resource header (the same image_blit path used for .pic backgrounds). The dest is NOT a per-slot rect — it is the whole 176x112 viewport, over which the walls are then composited.

findings.claim: Decoded the live 2-bit N/W wall grids for level 0 at the reference frame (party x7,y3,facing 0=+y). Values are dominated by 0 (open) and 2 (solid), with a few 3 (door/special). The party at (x7,y3) has N-wall row y3 entirely 0 (open corridor straight ahead, matching the receding corridor in the frame); the far cells ahead (y4..y7) have 2/3 closing off the corridor (the green gate). West-wall column x7 around y3 = 0; the side walls the player sees are the W-walls of the x7 column at y4+ and adjacent columns.

evidence.details:
Maze block near-ptr 0x4faa=0x7504. N-wall field at +0x60, W-wall at +0x120, 2 bits/cell MSB-first, cell=z*64+y*8+x. Level-0 N-wall grid (rows y0..y7, cols x0..x7):

  y1: 2 0 2 0 0 2 2 2
  y2: 2 0 2 2 2 2 2 2
  y3: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
  y4: 2 0 0 0 2 2 2 3
  y5: 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
  y6: 0 0 0 0 0 2 2 0
  y7: 2 0 0 0 2 0 2 3
Level-0 W-wall grid:
  y0: 0 2 0 2 0 0 0 0
  y1: 0 2 2 2 2 2 0 0
  y2: 0 0 0 0 2 2 2 0
  y3: 0 2 2 0 2 2 2 0
  y4: 0 2 2 0 2 2 2 0
  y5: 0 2 2 0 0 0 0 0

The party at (7,3) faces +y. Looking ahead the W-walls at x6/x7 rows y3,y4 = 2 (the converging side walls in the frame); the corridor terminates where the forward cells carry 2/3 (the green gate). Value 1 appears (W-wall y7 x4/x5) — so all of 0,1,2,3 occur. Earlier passes saw mostly 0/2/3; value 1 is confirmed present here.

findings.claim: Wall-bit value 0 = open/no wall (corridor sees through). Value 2 = solid stone wall (the dominant blocking wall and the one rendered in the static frame). Values 1 and 3 are special edge types (door/portcullis/secret) — value 3 sits exactly at the corridor-terminating cells around the green gate (N-wall y4 x7=3, y7 x7=3; W-wall y6 x1=3), and value 1 at W-wall y7 x4/x5. NOT FULLY PINNED: which of 1/3 is the visible green gate vs a one-way/secret edge, and the exact wall-value -> walltype-code mapping inside 0x3828.

evidence.details: Cross-referencing the decoded grids (finding maze-wall-bits-reference-frame) against the frame: the green portcullis terminates the corridor ahead of the party, and value 3 cells cluster at the corridor-end cells. Value 2 = the plain stone walls that fill most blocking edges. Confirm by driving free movement (read maze_can_step_in_facing 0x3244 per value) and by hand-tracing 0x3828's value->code switch.
